title: While Ask writes a long plan, its line names each step as it is written
goal: When Ask writes a big plan in one go (a sheet of components took 97 seconds on one answer), the Agent panel's live line names each part as the model writes it ('Writing the steps: Toggle, 4 so far') instead of sitting on 'Writing the steps' with only a clock, so a person can tell how far along it is.
notes:
Seen 2026-11-01 by while-ask-works-the-agent-panel-says-what-it-is. Command: a one-off walk running only 'create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text' at Next defaults (copy of the sheet block of Scripts/playtest/ask-says-what-it-is-doing-across-requests-walk.json). Its ask.stages: '88.3s Writing the steps', '185.5s Working out the steps' -> 97.2 s on one line (the line shows its time, 1:37, so the checklist's elapsed-time clause holds, but there is no sense of how far). The rotating check's run of the same request: 18.2 s on 'Writing the steps'.

Why it cannot say more today: the turn is one non-streamed POST (AskModelServer.chat -> AskLocalModel.send), and llama-server b11826's /slots gives only n_decoded (tokens written), never the text, so the steps are not known until the answer lands. The way in is streaming the chat (stream:true, SSE tool_call deltas from llama-server's OpenAI endpoint) and counting tool calls / reading each call's name or component name as it arrives, feeding AskStage (Sources/PhotonzCore/AskProgress.swift) a new .writing(step:name:) case. Keep the unreadable-reply path in AskSession.plan working.
acceptance: During a component sheet request, the line changes at least every 8 seconds while the model writes its answer, naming the step or part it has reached
Nothing about the finished result changes: the same requests make the same layers, and a reply the model breaks off part way is still handled as today
Measured on a component sheet and a fox drawing at Next defaults, with the longest gap recorded in an audit

log.note: Before building: a person watching a long plan wants to see it move and to recognise what is being made; the component names (Toggle, Button) are their words, the tool names are not, so the line names the step's own name and the part inside it, never a tool. Risk checked first: does streaming change the answer? Measured on llama-server b11826 (Qwen3.5 4B, temperature 0): streamed and unstreamed replies assemble to identical tool calls, for a whole answer and for one cut off by max_tokens; llama.cpp builds both from the same final parse, and a mid-stream complaint arrives as an 'error:' event with the same message, so the unreadable-reply path (Failed to parse tool call) still fires. Only the plan's turns stream; every other call to the server is unchanged. Chose 'Writing step 4: Toggle, Knob' over the task's 'Writing the steps: Toggle, 4 so far' because the step number first reads as progress and the name is what gets cut at the 40 character budget.

Measured at Next defaults (ask-names-each-step-as-it-writes-walk, Qwen3.8 27B): run 1 found a 22 s stall on 'Writing step 6: Segmented Control…' (long name cut over the part) and a step-0 flicker back to 'Reading your request' when /slots read late; both fixed and tested. Run 2: sheet writing 10.0-117.7 s, 11 steps, longest gap while writing 3.4 s (bar 8), whole request 7.3 s; fox one step, longest gap 4.0 s while painting, plans/paints/traces as before. Pictures looked at: 1-sheet-at-110s-sc.png (line reads 'Writing step 10: Alert, Success', mid-crossfade from 'Message') and 1-sheet-done-sc.png (full sheet, 83 layers). Left rough, not filed: Ollama runtime does not stream (still 'Writing the steps'); the line's crossfade is often caught mid-fade at this change rate. Commit 94516f463.

Ask's plan turns on the built-in model stream; the Agent line now says 'Writing step N: <name>, <part>' as the model writes. Same reply shape (tests + measured identical on b11826), unreadable-reply path intact. Measured: component sheet longest gap while writing 3.4 s (bar 8), fox 4.0 s overall. Audit queue/audits/2026-11-18-ask-names-each-step-as-it-writes.json; commit 94516f463.
